name: Hot Magenta
lede: Hot Magenta is a fluorescent-bright pink-violet, the color of 1970s punk lettering and the Crayola fluorescent box.

sections.title: Fluorescent, and loud
sections.body:
St Clair dates the color to the fluorescent craze of the 1970s, when brighter versions of the 1960s advertising and pop-art palette arrived [1]. In 1972 Crayola issued a special box of eight fluorescent crayons that included ultra pink and hot magenta, all glowing under black light [1]. The strident brashness suited punk, whose mohawks and album lettering used highly saturated fluorescent pinks [1].

The swatch on this page is the xkcd color survey's version of 2010, and ISCC-NBS would call it a deep purplish pink, though it sits some twelve units from that block's center [2]. The relatives are [[magenta]], [[hot-pink]] and [[fuchsia]] [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: No painting in our archive of 23,781 has this color across even one per cent of its canvas [3]. That describes museum paintings as photographed, not painting as a whole, and it is what a fluorescent color should show: it is a product of twentieth-century dyes and screens [3].
